- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 3–8% in subsequent days, especially if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was high recently — if so, assume model overreacted; apply mean reversion bias correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show downward trend + negative sentiment, model often fails to adjust — force a slight downward bias (−1 to −3%) in forecast.
- If sentiment is negative or volatile, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly (by 1–3%) to account for potential rebound.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed or low — model often overestimates momentum; cap upward revisions at 2% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If true outcome is consistently below 70% of forecast range, consider model is ignoring mean reversion — apply a 5–10% downward adjustment for next period.
